purpose: Produce the first reviewable native-scale Exilada body candidate from the user-locked pixel-art turnaround without reopening generation, model search, or manual repainting.

method_boundary.why_this_is_not_v3: V3 started from a high-resolution render and attempted to manufacture pixel art by reduction/quantization. V4 starts from the user's locked image that is already pixel-art imagery and performs only a bounded source-view extraction, conservative flat-background key, and nearest-neighbor scale normalization for review.
allowed: select the existing front-three-quarter pixel-art view from the locked four-view image
remove only the flat dark presentation background to alpha
normalize visible standing height to 128 px using nearest-neighbor only
preserve source RGB/value structure without palette synthesis
generate enlarged nearest-neighbor and 640x360 gameplay previews
hash and report the resulting candidate
forbidden: use the high-resolution photorealistic/anatomy render as visible sprite source
quantize or pixel-filter a smooth render into compliance
smooth, average or antialias during scaling
automatically promote the candidate without visual review

visual_pass: reads as intentional pixel art at native 1x rather than a reduced render
body silhouette remains recognizably the locked Exilada body
face, hands, feet, chest, pelvis and legs remain readable enough at native scale
value grouping remains coherent after scale normalization
retains mature severe sensual dangerous sword-and-sorcery presence
looks acceptable in the 640x360 gameplay preview
failure_policy: Close this normalization route if the native candidate visibly collapses or reads as filtered/reduced art. Do not ask the user for another reference and do not rescue it with anatomy/silhouette repair filters.
next_action: Run the approved V4 review runner once and inspect the contact sheet.
next_if_pass: Promote the accepted native candidate to the persistent B3B body source and add deterministic validation/export metadata before B4.
next_if_fail: Keep B3B current and revise the authoring implementation while preserving the fixed-reference lock.
